Your body age. One number, calculated from nine values in your blood, set against your age. Each body system, read for you. Where every result sits, what it means for your days, and what moves it. What connects. Your thyroid and your arteries, your sugar and your liver, read together as one body. Section 13 shows what connects in yours. Where to start. Three things, in order. A date to test again. So the next reading shows what changed. Alongside your 51 measured results, it works out 8 scores and your body age. 04 What your body age means Two people can share a birthday and not be the same age. Think of two people who are both 53. One takes the stairs without thinking and shakes off a cold in two days. The other is tired by mid-afternoon and takes a fortnight to recover. They have had the same number of birthdays. Their bodies have not aged at the same pace. Body age is a way of measuring that pace. Researchers in the United States took routine blood results from a large national health study and asked a simple question: which ordinary values best tell apart the people who stay well from the people who do not? Nine of them did most of the work. Read together with your age, they give the age your blood looks, whatever your birth certificate says. What the research found The measure was then checked in a second group of 11,432 adults, who were followed for about twelve years. Three things stood out. It tracked how people fared. Those whose body age ran behind their birthday tended to stay well for longer. Those whose body age ran ahead fared worse. The link held for younger and older adults, and across education and lifestyle. It saw what a routine check had not. The link held even among people who looked healthy, with no diagnosed disease and a normal weight. It moved with illness. The more conditions a person had, the older their body age read, step by step. What it means for you A body age of 42.8 at 53 does not promise ten extra years. It says that today your blood looks like that of a younger person in those studies. That is worth protecting. A tree lays down a ring every year: wide in a good year, narrow in a hard one. Your blood keeps a similar record, and unlike a birthday, the reading can move in either direction. If your markers improve, the number comes down with them. Nobody has yet shown that a lower number by itself means a longer life, so we use it as a direction to steer by and read it again at each test. What it does not tell you It does not read cholesterol. None of the nine values is a cholesterol number, so a young body age says nothing about your arteries. That is why this report reads the heart separately, and why yours can read ten years younger while your heart section still needs attention. It is not a diagnosis or a prediction for one person. It was built on a US population and is still being tested in others. Your age is itself one of the inputs. A cold, a hard workout or a poor night before the test can nudge a single reading, so the direction over two or three tests is what counts. What this section reads Cholesterol does not travel loose in the blood. It is carried in particles, and it is the number of particles, more than the amount of cholesterol, that decides how much ends up in artery walls. This section counts both, and adds the markers of inflammation and wear that decide how the artery wall copes. Your results · 13 markers, 1 in range ApoB the number of cholesterol-carrying particles 143.2 mg/dL middle zone 100 155 usual aim under 100 · lab range up to 155 LDL cholesterol the cholesterol inside those particles 142.6 mg/dL middle zone 100 160 under 100 ideal · 160 and over high Non-HDL cholesterol all the cholesterol that can enter an artery wall 174.7 mg/dL 9% above range 160 lab under 160 Total cholesterol everything added together 231 mg/dL middle zone 200 240 under 200 desirable · 240 and over high Triglycerides fat travelling in the blood 160.6 mg/dL middle zone 150 200 under 150 normal · 200 and over high HDL cholesterol cholesterol being carried away 56.3 mg/dL in range 40 lab over 40 ApoA1 the protective particles 102.2 mg/dL 15% below range 120 190 lab 120–190 ApoB to ApoA1 ratio calculated harmful particles against protective ones 1.4 56% above range 0.7 0.9 under 0.7 good · over 0.9 high Remnant cholesterol calculated what is left once HDL and LDL are taken out 32.1 mg/dL 7% above range 20 30 under 20 good · over 30 high Triglyceride to HDL ratio calculated a quick read of particle quality 2.86 middle zone 2.0 3.5 under 2.0 good · over 3.5 high Lp(a) an inherited particle, measured once 30.2 mg/dL just outside range 30 lab under 30 Homocysteine a marker of wear on the artery wall needs a deeper look 22.07 umol/L 47% above range 3.7 15 lab 3.7–15.0 hs-CRP background inflammation 2.09 mg/L middle zone 1.0 3.0 lab under 1.0 low · over 3.0 high What it means for you Today. You feel nothing. That is the difficulty with this one. Over the years. A heavy particle load is one of the patterns linked with heart disease later in life. It is also one of the most changeable. New in this report. A standard check-up counts the cholesterol. This counts the particles carrying it, and adds a second marker of artery wear. What to do. Food comes first, and that is where the work starts. Numbers at this level are also worth mentioning at your next routine check-up. What moves these numbers The kind of fat and fibre in your food, body weight, how well the thyroid is working, alcohol and sleep all move these numbers within months. Back to contents 08 Thyroid needs a deeper look The signal asking your thyroid to work harder is raised. What this section reads TSH is the signal your brain sends to ask the thyroid for more hormone. When it runs high, the thyroid is being pushed. T4 and T3 are the hormones it makes in reply. This report adds the free hormones, which are the part your cells can use. Your results · 5 markers, 4 in range TSH the signal asking the thyroid to work needs a deeper look 8.31 uIU/mL 89% above range 0.4 4.4 lab 0.40–4.40 T4, total the main hormone the thyroid makes 9.25 ug/dL in range 4.5 12.6 lab 4.5–12.6 T3, total the active hormone 113 ng/dL in range 60 210 lab 60–210 Free T4 the hormone your cells can actually use 0.91 ng/dL in range 0.61 1.12 lab 0.61–1.12 Free T3 the active form 3.23 pg/mL in range 2.6 4.2 lab 2.6–4.2 What it means for you Today. People with a raised signal often feel tired, cold or slower than they used to. What the deeper tests add. Your free hormones are in range. The signal is raised, but your thyroid is still keeping up. Whether your immune system is involved is the next thing to check. What to do. This needs a deeper look, read alongside your history: what is pushing the signal up while the hormones hold. A signal this far outside its range needs a doctor's attention as well, because medicine can be part of the answer. What moves these numbers Iodine, selenium and iron, long-term stress and some medicines all play a part. In a client's words “I began to understand the connection between my gut health and my skin condition, which gave me a whole new perspective on my wellbeing. And when I started changing my lifestyle and diet as per the guidance, the weight I had been struggling with for years started coming off more easily and stayed off as my thyroid numbers improved.” A client who started with a thyroid finding. Both thyroid antibodies were above the normal range at the start, and back inside it fourteen weeks later, at the same laboratory. Back to contents 11 Vitamins and iron watch Your vitamin D and iron are comfortably in range. Your B12 is well above it. What this section reads Vitamin D, vitamin B12 and iron are the reserves your energy, nerves and blood are built from. A standard panel rarely includes them, and each can run low or high for years without a symptom. Your reserves at a glance Your results · 6 markers, 5 in range Vitamin D (25-OH) 42.2 ng/mL in range 30 100 lab 30–100 Vitamin B12 1,475 pg/mL 62% above range 120 911 lab 120–911 Iron iron in the blood today 109.2 ug/dL in range 59 158 lab 59–158 Iron-binding capacity (TIBC) how much more iron the blood could carry 333.2 ug/dL in range 110 370 lab 110–370 Transferrin saturation how full your iron carriers are 32.8 % in range 16 50 lab 16–50 Phosphorus 3.8 mg/dL in range 2.5 5.0 lab 2.5–5.0 What it means for you Today. Nothing here is short. A B12 this high usually comes from supplements or fortified food. Why it matters in your report. Homocysteine normally comes down when B12 is plentiful. Yours is high while your B12 is full, so a shortage of B12 is not the explanation. That requires a deeper look and further investigation. What moves these numbers Sunlight and supplements for vitamin D. Diet, absorption and supplements for B12. Diet, blood loss and inflammation for iron. Back to contents 13 Reading it as one body Results are filed by organ. Bodies do not work that way, so here is what connects across sections. Thyroid and arteries. A raised thyroid signal and a raised particle load often travel together, because thyroid hormone helps the liver clear those particles from the blood. It is one reason the thyroid result comes first. Sugar and fats. Your triglycerides and your three-month sugar average are both a little high while your insulin is very low. That is an unusual pair. It is one to look at again at your next test before anyone acts on it. Homocysteine and B12. Your homocysteine is high although your B12 is well above range. With B12 this full, a simple shortage is unlikely to be the cause, so this pair needs a deeper look together. 14 Your next test 4 November 2026 Four months after this test, because this report has things to work on. When to come back If you work on this yourself: 4 November 2026. Four months is long enough for your artery load and your sugar average to show a change. If your thyroid is rechecked sooner: use that date. A change there can move your cholesterol too. When a report is steady all through: about a year is enough. Yours is not there yet. What to expect What can move in four months. The artery load, the sugar average and the inflammation. What we would hope to see. Your body age holding where it is, and the heart picture moving from “needs attention” towards “watch”. What will not move. One part of your heart picture is largely inherited (Lp(a) 30.2 mg/dL · lab under 30). It changes little, so there is no need to repeat it at four months. 15 What a functional health coach does Your doctor looks for disease and treats it. Nothing here replaces that.
